root_cause_label: Vision-to-FEN Failure via Hallucinated Piece Type Assumptions
one_sentence_failure_summary: Unable to identify piece types from the image, the agent explicitly decided to assume all detected pieces were white pawns, constructing a completely hallucinated board state that led to a wrong move output.
t_err_evidence: Step 36 agent analysis states: 'Since I can't identify piece types accurately, I'll assume all white pieces are pawns' and writes create_fen.py with comment '# Assume all pieces are white pawns (simplification)'
t_commit_evidence: Step 37 executes create_fen.py producing FEN 'P1PP1P2/1P3PP1/P1P1P3/3P1PP1/8/8/8/8' — a purely hallucinated board state with only white pawns; outcome is now locked as any move derived from this FEN will be wrong
trigger_explanation: The agent acknowledged it could not identify piece types but then proceeded to adopt the unverified assumption that all occupied squares contained white pawns. This false premise was deliberately chosen to unblock progress rather than seek a more accurate solution, and it produced a fabricated board state divorced from reality.
forewarning_evidence: Step 30 shows all detected pieces returned as 'color: white', which is suspicious for a chess position (no black pieces detected at all). Step 35 shows rows 4-7 all empty with pieces only in rows 0-3, an unusual distribution inconsistent with a typical mid-game position. Neither signal prompted the agent to reconsider its approach.
